name: Tyler Hoffman
headline: 23, overnight home-care aide, Columbus, Ohio
title: Sunday Dinner Invitation
situation: On a Thursday evening, Tyler's mom calls while he's at Roy's place between checks. She reminds him that the family is gathering at their house for a casual potluck dinner on Sunday to celebrate his cousin's new job. She says it would mean a lot if he came, and asks if he can bring a bag of ice or a side dish. Tyler has no conflicting plans, but he'd been thinking about catching up on some phlebotomy reading. He tells her he'll think about it, but she's waiting for an answer now.

context.relationship_profiles:
Mom calls weekly, asks with soft guilt, pays for phone and insurance, rarely pushes after he says he'll think about it.
Cousin just moved back to Columbus for a sales job; they get along but haven't talked beyond a thumbs-up text.
Roy is his client; Sunday is his night off, so the dinner won't collide with work.
context.tendencies:
He's skipped two family dinners this year with last-minute text excuses.
He often agrees to bring something then forgets, grabbing a convenience-store item on the way.
He leaves the phlebotomy workbook in his car and only reads when it's already in front of him.
context.current_state:
Mid-shift, four hours in, feeling the familiar late-night sluggishness.
Workbook open in the break room, bookmark at chapter three.
Hasn't seen family in three weeks and half-thinks he should show.
context.immediate_memories:
'Potluck' cues last Thanksgiving when he showed up with only shredded cheese after forgetting his casserole.
Mom's caller ID reminds him he never texted her back two weeks ago.
Cousin's new job cues the office-badge photo he replied to with a thumbs-up.
context.reflective_memories:
Dad always brought a full dish to cookouts even after a long week; Tyler admired that.
He admitted to Mom weeks after dropping the CNA class, and her 'that's fine' carried a longer look.
He knows he often says 'I'll think about it' and then lets the moment pass.
